A very warm welcome
Chesham Prep is a unique co-educational school where children benefit from an exceptional learning environment and a kaleidoscope of experiences that make a lifetime of difference. Children thrive through the combination of small, focused classroom sizes, visionary teaching and the freedom to explore in wide open green spaces. The pupils’ interest in and excitement and energy for learning and experimenting is palpable throughout the school and enables them to achieve outstanding results at 11+ and beyond.

Our Facilities
In our idyllic, 13 acre semi-rural setting outside of Chesham, pupils are exposed to a wide variety of stimulating and reflective environments where they have the freedom to broaden their minds, express their creativity, release their imagination and develop their physical abilities.

pageCache.text:
Languages and International Awareness at Chesham Prep
Throughout their time at Chesham Prep, children are introduced to and learn French and Spanish, with 1 lesson a week until Year 6, when pupils increase to 3 lessons a week. We see languages as a pivotal and extremely beneficial part of the curriculum at Chesham Prep, helping to improve all-around cognitive skills as well as enhancing soft skills such as problem-solving, empathising with others and critical thinking.
In the early years, children learn Spanish and French through song, dance and play and tactile learning experiences. Every lesson, led a specialist teacher, focuses on being fully immersive, enjoyable and fun where the enjoyment is key. Connecting new language to familiar activities – food likes and dislikes; traditional and joyful celebrations as well as through games and dance allows new language to bed in, almost without the children realising it. This bedrock of playful learning provides a strong base for when a more structured approach is introduced in Year 2 onwards, when the focus turns to the four key skills of listening, reading, speaking and writing.
From Years 2-4 the children take their foreign language learning back into the home with our Language bags programme. The bag contains games, a book and a simple recipe for the child to prepare. Enjoyable activities which again ensure full immersion and enjoyment. This approach continues to run into Year 6, where the pupils run a French market for the day.
By the time children reach Years 5 and 6, they are ready to explore their skills with the outside world. A trip abroad to either Spain or France in Year 5 and 6 further develops language abilities, as does our annual participation in the UK Linguistics Olympiad, a national competition which challenges pupils to solve linguistic puzzles, developing their logical thinking as well as their language capabilities. We celebrate the myriad of languages exhibited at both this event as well as at the European Day of Languages each September. Our participation in all of these additional learning opportunities, has allowed us to work towards full accreditation of the Intermediate International Schools Award.
Through steady, incremental and always enjoyable learning steps, children are well prepared for language studies at secondary school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing Arts | Independent School, Bucks | Chesham Prep
pageCache.text:
Music at Chesham Prep
At Chesham Prep, music isn’t just a subject, it’s a core part of school life and a pillar of our exceptional performing arts provision. Every child, from Nursery to Year 6, receives specialist music lessons twice a week, led by our experienced and passionate music teachers. From the first beat to the final performance, our pupils are immersed in a rich, joyful musical curriculum that builds confidence, creativity and technical skill.
Our dedicated music department is well-equipped, with class sets of ukuleles, glockenspiels, djembes, MIDI keyboards and SoundTrap for digital composition, ensuring that children experience both traditional and contemporary music-making. Whether it’s singing in harmony, mastering rhythm or composing their own pieces, pupils grow into capable, expressive musicians.
A School Where Every Child Performs
From the earliest years, all pupils take part in concerts, nativities, and full-scale musical productions, building stage presence, performance skills and a true love for the arts. Our five school choirs, including the auditioned Senior Choir and inclusive Singing for Wellbeing clubs, offer outstanding opportunities for vocal development, while a range of instrumental ensembles, including Orchestra, Wind, Strings, Brass and Guitar Ensembles, ensure that musicians of every level are supported and challenged.
Specialist Tuition & Musical Excellence
We deliver over 170 individual music lessons every week through a talented team of visiting professionals. Our pupils thrive under expert guidance, preparing for ABRSM music exams which can be taken right here on site, thanks to our status as an official ABRSM exam centre. This ensures every child benefits from a familiar, supportive setting as they progress through their musical journey.
Productions
At Chesham Prep, our exceptional performing arts programme shines through in full-scale school productions in Year 4 and Year 6, complete with an exciting array of costumes, props, singing, dancing and ensemble performance. These high-energy, confidence-building shows give every child a chance to shine on stage or behind the scenes, developing creativity, public speaking skills, teamwork, and a lifelong love of the arts. It’s a highlight of our vibrant curriculum and a key reason families choose our school for its outstanding performing arts opportunities.
Drama at Chesham Preparatory School
At Chesham Preparatory School, our drama curriculum is designed to nurture confidence, creativity, and collaboration. Through drama, pupils develop essential skills in teamwork and communication, as well as the courage to take creative risks, qualities that enrich their learning across all subjects.
Our programme also fosters cultural literacy, encouraging pupils to become curious, reflective, and active thinkers who appreciate the power of performance and storytelling.
Performance is at the heart of our drama curriculum. From class assemblies and year-group productions to whole-school events and community celebrations, pupils have regular opportunities to perform and share their talents. These experiences grow in scale and ambition as children progress through the school, culminating in the highly anticipated Senior Production- a celebration of their achievements in acting, singing, and dance.
LAMDA
Our co-curricular LAMDA programme offers pupils a unique platform to further explore acting, public speaking, and technical performance techniques, gaining recognised qualifications along the way. Whether nurturing futures in acting or enhancing everyday presentation skills, LAMDA empowers every pupil to express themselves and gain valuable skills and experiences.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sports | Independent Prep School, Bucks | Chesham Prep
pageCache.text:
Sport forms an important part of life at Chesham Prep School. From Nursery all of our children get to experience a wide variety of different sporting activities through PE and games lessons as well as in a wide variety of clubs.
The ethos of the sports department is very much one that every child will be given the opportunity to develop their potential to the very best of their abilities. With this in mind, the children receive coaching from experienced teachers, each with their own fields of expertise. All children get the opportunity to play in competitive matches, through fixtures against other schools from Year 3 and during our House competitions. Results are not our main priority; developing well rounded and skilled individuals who are able to be creative, make decisions for themselves and self-organise are the focus of our pupil centres approach.
Our aim is that all children leave us with a love of sport and a desire to continue participating which will stay with them throughout their life.
PE
Physical Education is an important part of the curriculum at Chesham Prep School. All pupils receive a PE lesson each week where we focus on developing fundamental skills through a broad and enriching programme. Whilst we develop their physical fitness and skill acquisition, we also encourage them to develop their social and mental well-being by challenging them to overcome adversity, work effectively as part of a group and enjoy the spirit of competition. Our PE curriculum includes sports such as Basketball, Gymnastics and Parkour, Dance, SAQ, ‘Beat the Game’ and Health Related Fitness.
Games
Games is an exciting part of what is offered at Chesham Prep School. All pupils from Year 3 – 6 take part in two games lessons a week. For the boys the main sports are Rugby, Football and Cricket whilst the girls compete in Hockey, Football, Netball and Cricket. We endeavour to provide every child with a fixture each week in which they can put the different individual and unit skills they have been developing into practice in a competitive environment.
Our approach to games is to provide an environment in which pupils feel that they can be creative and try things and we look to avoid a fear of failure attitude within the pupils. Whilst competition is healthy and teaches them the value of victory and defeat, the learning that can take place within fixtures is more important than the result.
Children are encouraged to work together for a common aim as well as developing individual targets. The school has high expectations of all of our children; that they will display excellent levels of courtesy, good manners and a high level of sportsmanship at all times, whilst being good guests or hosts.
Parent support is always welcomed at fixtures and helps to create the encouraging and enthusiastic environment in which the pupils excel.
Swimming
Weekly 40-minute lessons take place in our beautiful, heated 25-metre pool for pupils in Years 1–6, with Reception children beginning their swimming journey in the summer term. From Reception to Year 4, children progress through the CPS badge scheme, earning certificates and badges as their skills develop, while parents can track progress and receive updates via our online portal. In Years 5 and 6, pupils broaden their aquatic expertise through half-term modules in water safety and water polo. We also host swimming galas with local schools and have a strong competitive record, having previously reached national finals held at the Olympic Pool and Ponds Forge. Recreational clubs and squad training for Years 3–6 provide further opportunities for children to enjoy additional pool time and excel in the water.

pageCache.pageTitle: House System | Independent School, Bucks | Chesham Prep
pageCache.text:
Key to life at Chesham Prep is the house system.
Our four school houses, Aylward, Attenborough, Nightingale and Stevenson, are each named after pioneering individuals who possess the strengths, abilities, gifts and talents that inspire future generations of children. Each House fundraises throughout the year to make donations to a selected house charity.
Children are allocated to and remain part of one of the four school Houses from Reception until Year 6. Vertical tutor groups are held for House meetings and House events engendering an “across the years” experience for pupils with senior prep pupils showing the way and encouraging younger house members. We ensure families, including Alumni, are in the same house.
Rivalry between Houses is healthily competitive, and centres around the rewards system for House points. These are awarded for many acts of kindness (such as helping others, politeness) and achievement (times tables rock stars, Inter-House sports competitions). Regular updates and tallies are announced at key school events and at Speech Day the overall winner is announced. The triumphant House Captains have the honour of lifting the House Cup in front of the whole school.
Aylward
Gladys Aylward (1902-1970) was an English missionary in China and Taiwan who worked to end the traditional Chinese practice of binding women’s feet, led a large group of orphans out of occupied China, and set up orphanages in Hong Kong and Taiwan.
Gladys was a remarkable woman. She was determined and had remarkable faith. Despite being a poorly educated parlour maid rejected by a missionary society because she failed the exams she became a widely respected heroic missionary in China and transformed so many lives.
Attenborough
In 2024, listening to the pupil’s voice, a new name was chosen to replace the original House Columbus. After a pupil vote, the runaway winner was Attenborough after Sir David Attenborough.
Sir David Attenborough is a famous English naturalist and broadcaster known for his amazing nature documentaries that show the world’s animals and plants to millions of people. Many children recognize and love his calm, distinctive voice as he shares stories about the natural world. He has been exploring and explaining the natural world for more than 60 years, making him a beloved icon for many generations.
His passion for the natural world encourages children to appreciate and protect the environment which makes him an ideal Chesham Prep House ambassador.
Nightingale
Florence Nightingale was a famous British nurse who founded modern nursing and proved that cleanliness and fresh air could save lives. She dedicated her life to helping others despite her wealthy upbringing and was determined to improve healthcare for everyone.
She is best known for her work during the Crimean War, where she led a team of nurses into a dirty, crowded military hospital. By making changes like washing hands and cleaning the wards, she drastically reduced the number of soldiers who died from infections, earning her the nickname “The Lady with the Lamp” for her nightly rounds checking on patients. After the war, she used her influence and fame to push for hospital reforms and establish the world’s first professional nursing school.
Stevenson
Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish writer known for classics like Treasure Island and Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde. He was special for his vivid storytelling, adventurous spirit, and ability to explore deep human themes. Despite poor health, he wrote stories that still captivate readers today.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our History & Alumni | Prep School, Bucks | Chesham Prep
pageCache.text:
Chesham Preparatory School was founded in Station Road, Chesham, in 1938 by Mrs Christina Adlington, a qualified teacher who had moved to Buckinghamshire from London. Together with her husband, Ernest, Mrs Adlington soon assembled a dedicated team of people with the talent and enthusiasm to make a success of the new enterprise. The outbreak of war and its evacuees brought a large influx of people into Chesham, and a new facility to accommodate greater pupil numbers was required. In May 1940, the School moved to its current site, which it has continued to develop to meet the needs of subsequent generations of pupils.
Mrs Adlington always intended Chesham Prep to be an independent school for boys and girls of “ordinary, diligent families” – something apart from prep schools for the very wealthy – and, ever since, it has enabled parents from a cross-section of the community to choose independent education in a school with a friendly, family atmosphere and a Christian background. This ethos is reflected in the founding motto of the School – “Each for all and All for each”. We remember this day to day but particularly on Founder’s Day, celebrated every spring,
The school has grown considerably since those early days but remains true to its original ambition of providing a caring and nurturing environment where children aim high, work hard and achieve great things. We have a special community that endures through generations, as well as welcoming newcomers each and every year. We remain in contact with many of our alumni, from those who were first evacuated in the 1940’s, to our most recent school leavers.
We would love to hear from anyone who has spent time at Chesham Prep, whether you were at the school from the beginning in the 1940’s or have only just left us last year. Please fill out the Alumni Contact Form below to join our Alumni community and we shall keep you informed of any future events.
Please contact us by emailing lelms@cheshamprep.co.uk if you have any fond memories you would like to share.

Art is presented in a lively and interesting way throughout the school where children learn with using new materials discovery and an increasing use of knowledge and skills.
The school has a specialised Art and Design Room with an extensive range of facilities including a kiln, screen printing, and silk painting.
The Art syllabus provides a broad range of opportunities where each year group learn by using new materials and acquiring new skills:
Design and Technology
Design and Technology is taught throughout Chesham Preparatory school from Nursery to Year 6. In Years 5 and 6 the pupils have the opportunity to work in the in the specialist technology room. Our pupils are put in charge of their own Design and Make projects, encouraging them to value their ideas and choices. They also work in groups where ideas are put forward and adapted whilst at the same time they learn to operate as part of a team to produce an end product.
There are close subject links with Science and Maths where pupils can cement academic ideas in practical tasks.

At Chesham Prep we understand how important wraparound care in a safe and happy environment is for many families. We provide a Breakfast Club service and two after school clubs – all are accessible to every pupil in the school.
This is in addition to the after school activity clubs.
The supervisory staff are fully trained and qualified and provide an interesting and varied programme of activities for the children.
